The same model as below, given the memory to hold a whole book of context at once. On a 48 GB machine the spare RAM is better spent on context than on precision — you can hand it an entire contract or a year of notes and it keeps all of it in view.

Planning aid only. The crane's own load chart and computer (LMI), the manufacturer's manuals and a competent lift planner always decide. Every rule here takes the cautious side.
{g} t of {c} t = {p}% of the chart
Estimated as 75% of crane + counterweight + load on one corner — cautious; use the real figure when you have it.
Mat needed: at least {a} m² — e.g. {s} × {s} m
The mat must be stiff enough to spread the load over its whole area (timber or steel mats of the right thickness).
Angle of each leg from vertical: {a}° (between legs: {b}°)
All legs share the load (engineered, balanced lift only)
Angle factor ×{f} · counted as {c} legs carrying
3- and 4-leg slings are rated as if only 2 legs carry the load — they rarely share it evenly.
Above 45° the tension rises fast — use longer slings or a spreader beam.
More than 60° from vertical is not allowed — longer slings or a spreader beam.
